title: The Return of the German Question
content: Until this month, a far-right, openly ethnonationalist party had never come so close to winning an absolute majority in an election in the Federal Republic of Germany. Now that it has, and with similarly pro-Russian forces on the rise in France, all Europeans must prepare for the worst.

title: UN Peacekeeping in Crisis
content: With the world facing the largest number of armed conflicts since 1946, the Trump administration’s continuing assault on the United Nations has prevented the organization from fulfilling its peacekeeping duties. A recent report by UN Secretary-General António Guterres shows how the organization has few, if any, levers to fight back.

title: Lies, Election Lies, and Trump’s Statisticians
content: An obviously amateurish brief published by the US Census Bureau should raise alarms for all businesses, investors, and others who rely on official government statistics. By recklessly undermining trust in what should be an apolitical public service, Donald Trump is jeopardizing a critical pillar of American prosperity.

title: The Return of the IMF to Latin America
content: Over the past decade, many Latin American and Caribbean countries internalized IMF-style policy discipline without having active IMF programs, producing fragile stagnation—and an opening for the Fund to swoop back in. This could end up helping the United States reassert its dominance over the region.

title: The AI Plot Thickens
content: When it comes to AI, it is difficult to know what to believe. Are the CEOs, researchers, and investors who tout the technology’s seemingly unlimited capabilities more credible, because they work directly with it, or less credible, because they stand to profit handsomely from further investment? While misplaced optimism could fuel a financial bubble, we have seen in recent months that underestimating the risks posed by AI could also carry other, even existential, costs.

title: How Trade Deals Can Save Nature
content: Environmental conservation is among the most important, universally shared imperatives the world faces, and market access is one of the few carrots available in international politics. By linking tariffs to deforestation, the EU and others can create trade agreements that deliver more conservation and more gains from trade.

title: Europe’s Third Way on China
content: Instead of choosing between a confrontation with China and business as usual, European policymakers should examine the benefits and costs of trade sector by sector to identify where mutually beneficial arrangements remain possible. Economic modeling shows that pragmatism beats more extreme options in most cases.

title: Alarm Bells in the Balkans
content: Recent developments in the Balkans ought to be a wake-up call for Europe, given the potential for nationalist provocations in one country to spill over within the region. Multiple elections coming next month raise the risk of a dangerous descent into political instability.

title: Trump’s 21st-Century Mercantilism
content: Since his return to the White House, Donald Trump has turned his back on the free-market principles that the United States spent decades championing. In doing so, he threatens to dismantle the economic order that helped produce unprecedented growth in global output and trade.

title: The AI Productivity Delusion
content: As with previous technological revolutions, it is natural to focus on AI's net effects: Will it create more than it destroys? But unlike previous eras of creative destruction, the real question this time is, “Create more of what?”

title: Preventing an AI World War
content: Warnings that AI may lead to our extinction often overlook the most immediate risk: a war triggered by an attack that no human intended or approved. A mechanism for distinguishing unintended harm from deliberate attacks is urgently needed.

title: Post-Liberal Europe?
content: Another victory for the far right in a German state election has confirmed European liberals' worst fears. With many critical European elections approaching in 2027, debates about the proper limits of popular sovereignty and other fundamental tenets of liberalism are now of paramount importance.

title: Germany’s Moment of Reckoning
content: As its growth model runs out of road, Germany must decide whether to defend aging industries or enable new ones to emerge. To translate its research excellence into globally competitive companies, it needs deeper capital markets and a genuine European single market in which promising startups can grow.

title: The Middle Powers Are Now the “Free World”
content: Europe, Canada, and the democracies of Africa, Asia, and Latin America now bear the burden of keeping the old American ideal of the free world alive. While the ideal was always a noble lie, it enabled hundreds of millions of people to imagine a better world during the Cold War, and it could do so again.

title: The Un-Ordered UN Order
content: As European leaders hobnob with their counterparts at the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly, they must think carefully about how to navigate a fast-changing multilateral landscape. The old world belonged to rule-makers and institution-builders, but the current one favors those who can improvise.

title: AI Needs Trusted Journalism
content: As people increasingly rely on AI chatbots for news, the already tenuous bargain between publishers and tech firms—the former invested in journalism that the latter helped audiences discover—is no longer workable. UNESCO’s proposed Guidance on Fair Compensation for News could help create a new value-exchange model.

title: How to Stop the AI-pocalypse
content: AI could very well end democracy, if not humanity, yet efforts to slow its development may fail as companies and countries race to stay ahead. Preventing such a future will require international coordination and taxing the extreme wealth that could put unprecedented power in the hands of a tiny elite.

title: What Killed Liberalism?
content: There is no shortage of people and ideas to blame for liberalism’s decline, but searching for a single culprit is probably futile. Two new books by Gordon Brown and Daron Acemoglu take up the harder question of how to rebuild the institutions that once gave people a sense of community and power over their lives.

title: Will AI Take Asian Young People’s Jobs?
content: While AI is beginning to affect some entry-level jobs, its effects remain limited and uneven, and there is little evidence of economy-wide displacement. Nonetheless, from updating education and training to strengthening labor-market institutions, policies are needed to support workers amid AI-induced disruption.

title: Technological Leapfrogging in the AI Age
content: Across Africa, past success stories have led policymakers to believe that developing economies can usually bypass the arduous, expensive stages of infrastructure development by adopting technologies built elsewhere. But this approach deserves more scrutiny, especially when applied to imported AI systems.
